To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of agency staff in core professional positions is problematic, that the problems associated with this are potentially serious, that there are ways of managing these problems, but that there are also constraints on the ability of public sector organizations to do so.
the increasing use of agency workers in public services has a negative impact on the quality of services and on the public service employment model.

agency workers are being used to fill core professional social work roles, that this is leading to a number of negative outcomes for the quality of the services provided and the employment conditions of the agency workers concerned, and that there are a number of constraints on the public agencies involved that limit their ability to manage these negative outcomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the implications of a growing trend for the future of professional employment in public services.
the implications of a new form of employment for public service employment models.
the implications of agency working in public services, and the extent to which this practice can be reconciled with the public service model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of agency professionals is not a good idea.
there are significant problems in the use of agencies, but that these are not insurmountable.
the use of agency staff is problematic and should be avoided.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the current growth of agency workers in public sector organizations has the potential to undermine the quality of public services, and to erode the foundations of a functional public service employment model.
the use of agency labour is a double-edged sword for organizations.
while there is no evidence to suggest that the use of agency staff has led to a wholesale erosion of public service employment models, it does pose challenges to them that need to be addressed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
agency workers may be a necessary part of the solution to public service employment problems, but they are not a panacea.
the use of agency staff to fill core professional positions is a potentially serious threat to public service employment models.
agency workers are not a neutral or benign form of labour.
